text:
incident-bot: PAGE: sudden surge of 429s observed on /v1/generate (canary) - paging oncall
Sam: I see the page, jumping in. which release pushed this morning?
Lee: saw canary alerts ~09:12 - token accounting mismatches in traces, lots of exemptions missing
Sam: @deploy-bot who deployed the ratecap change?
deploy-bot: deploy completed: rl-ratecap-refactor-canary by ci/cd at 2026-03-15T09:12:03Z
Maria: that refactor tightened some exemption logic for public vs dedicated tiers, intended to reduce token leakage for free tier
Alex: support: tickets spiking, multiple enterprise customers reporting 429s and failed gens, escalating to SOC
Sam: grabbing logs from canary nodes now. seeing many entries with exemption=null even for known dedicated customers
Sam: sample:
```
[2026-03-15T09:18:21Z] req=abcd1234 node=canary-a status=429 reason=rate_limited exemption=null tokens=230 account=d-edf
[2026-03-15T09:18:23Z] req=abcd9999 node=canary-b status=429 reason=rate_limited exemption=null tokens=480 account=d-acme
```
Lee: traces show exemption-matcher returned 204 for those calls earlier, but new code path isn't attaching exemption_id to accounting layer
Maria: consequence = dedicated accounts throttled incorrectly; risk of token accounting drift if counters didn't decrement
Sam: severity P1 -> immediate mitigation options: 1) flip feature flag on canary (kill-switch) 2) rollback canary image 3) global flip
Sam: prefer kill-switch for canary first, then rollback if persists
Sam: @deploy-bot run: featureflag disable rl-ratecap-refactor --scope=canary
deploy-bot: featureflag rl-ratecap-refactor set to disabled on scope=canary by Sam
Sam: monitoring 60s
Alex: support drafted customer note: short, apologetic, we're investigating and toggling an internal flag. Escalated to top-5 customers personally
Lee: 45s after toggle - 429 rate trending down but some stragglers remain
Sam: starting canary rollback in parallel to be safe
deploy-bot: rollback started: rl-ratecap-refactor-canary -> rl-ratecap-stable by Sam
Sam: rollback finished on canary nodes; verification logs show exemptions attached again
Sam: post-rollback sample:
```
[2026-03-15T09:21:12Z] req=ijkl9012 node=canary-a status=200 exemption=dedicated-42 tokens=230 account=d-edf
```
Maria: great. we need a quick ledger diff to ensure no customer token counters are inconsistent. Lee, can you run a counters audit?
Lee: running diff against pre-deploy snapshot -> current counters within +/- 2 tokens on sample accounts; full audit queued, will mark follow-up action
Alex: notified affected customers: 2 enterprise account owners got direct outreach, broader note sent to orgs impacted
Sam: filing incident ticket and adding rollback timeline. Handoff to next oncall in 45m for continued monitoring
Maria: immediate follow-ups: fix exemption attachment bug, add unit/integration test for exemption->accounting handoff, block canary promotion until gating checks pass
Lee: will add automated canary check to detect exemption_id absence for known dedicated accounts during rollout
Sam: creating postmortem skeleton and scheduling RFC for release checklist updates
PagerDuty: incident acknowledged by Sam
support: ongoing ticket triage, will update if any customer shows token discrepancy
Sam: last check - 429s at baseline across canary and staging; CPU/mem normal
Sam: closing page as mitigated, will keep incident open for postmortem and tests. timeline and logs attached to ticket 3150004321
